title: BMW Finance - Adapted Practice Example
effect: Customer dissatisfaction with wear and tear and residual value

causes.text: Vehicle assessors do not inform customers about the next steps.
causes.hint: People fits the assessor's communication. Procedure is also reasonable if the issue is a missing communication step.

causes.text: The independent assessor is considered biased.
causes.hint: The issue concerns the assessor's perceived impartiality, so People is the intended category. Bias is a perception to investigate, not an established fact.

causes.text: The dealership assessor estimates residual value lower than the value shown later in the official letter.
causes.hint: People fits inconsistent assessments. Procedure also fits if assessment guidance or the communication sequence is inconsistent. The statement does not identify the underlying mechanism.

causes.text: Customers receive no information about signs of use and decreased vehicle value.
causes.hint: Procedure fits a missing explanation in the return process. People also fits if staff fail to communicate the required information.

causes.text: Customers receive no information about how residual value is calculated.
causes.hint: Procedure fits a missing explanation of the calculation. People also fits if the problem is staff communication or knowledge.

causes.text: Evaluation of damage takes too long.
causes.hint: Procedure fits delays in the evaluation workflow. Systems also fits a processing or information-system bottleneck. Timing alone does not establish the root cause.

causes.text: The return protocol is sent by mail or fax, with no electronic distribution.
causes.hint: This statement explicitly describes the information-distribution channels. Systems is the intended category; the statement does not establish that these channels cause delays.
Procedure fits mistakes in preparing or checking the report. Systems also fits errors generated by the reporting system. No equipment failure is described.

causes.text: Goodwill allowances for wear and tear are handled too strictly.
causes.hint: Rules governing allowances and exceptions are Policy. The concern is how strictly goodwill allowances are applied.

causes.text: The return protocol, including damage information, is sent to customers too late.
causes.hint: Procedure fits a delay in preparing or sending the report. Systems also fits a distribution-system delay. The statement does not describe a policy requirement.

causes.text: Competitors offer vouchers for car damage or insurance.
causes.hint: Competitors' offers are external market conditions, so Environment is the intended category.

causes.text: Customers do not understand the acronyms in the return protocol.
causes.hint: Procedure fits unclear wording or a missing explanation in the document process. People also fits a customer-knowledge or communication gap. Nothing here identifies faulty equipment.

causes.text: Documents are incomplete when sent to SF.
causes.hint: Incomplete documents point to preparation, completeness checks, or handoff steps in the workflow. Procedure is the intended category for this wording; no equipment fault is described.

sub_causes.text: Calculation of residual value takes longer.
sub_causes.explanation: A smaller branch connected to incomplete documents. The connection is retained from the source example; confirm the intended causal direction before treating it as an established causal relationship.
